subject: Computer Science
instructions:
Operating systems final, topics to prepare:
- Difference between a process and a thread
- The four necessary conditions for deadlock
- Paging versus segmentation
- How round-robin scheduling works
- What a semaphore is and how it prevents race conditions
draft:
A process has its own address space. Threads live inside a process and share its memory, so switching between threads is cheaper.
Deadlock conditions: mutual exclusion and hold-and-wait.
Paging splits memory into fixed-size pages, which avoids external fragmentation. Segmentation uses variable-size logical units such as code and stack, so it can fragment.
Round robin gives each ready process a fixed time slice, then moves it to the back of the queue.
notes: Two of four deadlock conditions; semaphores absent.
